title: Ode to Joy (Beethoven)
note: The famous theme in four-part harmony; the top line is the tune. Stepwise and singable: the easiest melody on the list to recognise. Works as a title, a level-clear or an ending. Slow it down for solemn, speed it up for celebration.

title: Eine kleine Nachtmusik, 1st movement (Mozart)
note: Fanfare-like opening (a rising arpeggio answered by a falling one) then a lyrical second theme. Elegant and bright; good for a town, a palace or a confident title.

title: Piano Sonata K.331, theme (Mozart)
note: A siciliano-like 6/8 theme in A major: gentle and sweet. A fine hub, village or "a quiet day" tune; also the theme of a set of six variations if you want a game that develops one tune.

title: Rondo alla Turca (Mozart)
note: Fast, bouncy, "Turkish" (the left hand imitates drums). Great for chases, markets, caper levels. The A section is the famous part; the left hand is busy, so the arp voice is thin.

title: Gigue in G (Mozart)
note: A short, dancing gigue with quick contrapuntal lines; compound time. Use for a lively exploration stage.

title: Austria / Emperor's Hymn (Haydn)
note: A stately hymn tune (also the German anthem melody). Good for a ceremony, a coronation, a credits roll. Slow and square: easy to loop.

title: Music for the Royal Fireworks, Réjouissance (Handel)
note: A trumpet-led celebration; bright and brisk. Use for a victory screen or a festival level.

title: Minuet in E-flat, WoO 82 (Beethoven)
note: A courtly minuet in 3/4: relaxed, elegant. For a manor, a ballroom or a gentle puzzle.

title: Minuet in G (Petzold, in Anna Magdalena's notebook, long attributed to J. S. Bach)
note: The best-known beginner minuet. Simple, clear, perfectly suited to four-channel playback. Note: this is the Anna Magdalena Notebook minuet (BWV Anh. 114), now attributed to Christian Petzold; the Mutopia edition is public domain.
composer: Christian Petzold (c. 1677–1733), long attributed to J. S. Bach

title: Bist du bei mir (BWV 508, attributed to Stölzel)
note: A tender slow aria. Good for an ending, a lullaby moment, a loving story beat.
composer: Gottfried Heinrich Stölzel (1690–1749), long attributed to J. S. Bach

title: Sheep May Safely Graze (J. S. Bach, from BWV 208)
note: A serene pastoral in 3/8-like lilt with a gentle flowing bass. Ideal for a farm, a garden, a sleeping village.

title: Prelude in C major, WTC I (J. S. Bach)
note: Pure broken chords. There is no melody on top, so the "lead" will be the top note of each chord: a gentle, constantly moving background (great under puzzle or exploration). Use the lead and bass only; skip the arp voice.

title: Air on the G string (J. S. Bach)
note: A slow, singing melody over a walking bass. Solemn and beautiful; for an emotional ending or a night scene.

title: Maple Leaf Rag (Joplin)
note: The classic ragtime: a syncopated melody over an oom-pah bass. Ragtime suits platformers, towns and comic scenes. The left hand is a steady alternation of bass and chord, which maps well to bass + arp.

title: The Easy Winners (Joplin)
note: A swaggering ragtime with a lively, hummable first strain.

title: Elite Syncopations (Joplin)
note: Quick, syncopated and bright; the rhythm is the hook.

title: Peacherine Rag (Joplin)
note: A sunny ragtime, a little gentler than Maple Leaf; good for a friendly town.

title: Pineapple Rag (Joplin)
note: Bright and busy ragtime with a quick left hand.

title: Sun Flower Slow Drag (Joplin, with Scott Hayden)
note: A "slow drag": relaxed and swaying. A good easy-going town or beach hub.

title: Solace, a Mexican serenade (Joplin)
note: A tender habanera rhythm under a singing melody: gentle, a little wistful. Good for a calm evening scene.

title: Bethena, a concert waltz (Joplin)
note: A sweet-sad waltz; a good emotional stage or ending.

title: A Breeze from Alabama (Joplin)
note: Cheerful ragtime with a springy step.

title: The Liberty Bell march (Sousa)
note: A brisk, bright march. Marches have clear repeating phrases that loop well; good for a parade, a title, or a quick-paced stage.

title: El Capitan march (Sousa)
note: A swashbuckling march with a lively trio.

title: Hands Across the Sea (Sousa)
note: A proud, stately march; slower and more ceremonial than the others.

title: King Cotton march (Sousa)
note: A jaunty march.

title: The Gladiator march (Sousa)
note: A driving, heroic march; fits an arena or a "here we go" stage.

title: Gymnopédie No. 1 (Satie)
note: Slow waltz with a floating melody over alternating bass and chord. A model of what four channels do well: leave lots of space. Use it quiet and very slow; the lead is sparse.

title: Gymnopédie No. 2 (Satie)
note: A gentler sibling of No. 1, in C major. Slow and sparse.

title: Gymnopédie No. 3 (Satie)
note: The most melancholy of the three. Very sparse.

title: Clair de lune (Debussy, Suite bergamasque)
note: Moonlight itself. The famous melody enters after a short introduction; it is slow and spacious, with soft arpeggios. Debussy died in 1918. For a night, a lake, a quiet emotional moment.

title: Première arabesque (Debussy)
note: Flowing broken chords with a graceful melody. A gentle, moving background for exploration.

title: Träumerei (Schumann, Kinderszenen)
note: The classic "Dreaming": a long, singing line over soft harmony. Slow and beautiful; very good for an emotional ending.

title: Of Foreign Lands and Peoples (Schumann, Kinderszenen)
note: A gentle, curious tune about faraway places: a good "map" or "a journey begins" theme.

title: Glückes genug (Schumann, Kinderszenen)
note: "Happy enough": warm, simple and content.

title: Wiegenlied / Cradle Song (Schubert)
note: A lullaby with a rocking accompaniment. For a bedtime scene or a sleep screen.

title: Ave Maria (Schubert, Ellens dritter Gesang)
note: A flowing, serene hymn-like melody over arpeggios. Solemn and calming.

title: Heidenröslein (Schubert)
note: A simple strophic folk-style song: very easy to loop. For a meadow or a village.

title: Du bist die Ruh (Schubert)
note: A slow, tender, serene song.

title: Auf dem Wasser zu singen (Schubert)
note: The accompaniment ripples like water: for a lake, a river or a boat. The 6/8 rocking figure is the point; the melody floats over it.

title: An die Musik (Schubert)
note: A warm, noble song to music itself; a good menu or credits tune.

title: Die Forelle / The Trout (Schubert)
note: A playful tune with a darting piano figure (the trout in the stream). For a stream, a fishing stage, a light-hearted level.

title: Prelude Op. 28 No. 4 (Chopin)
note: Slow and heavy, a sinking left-hand chord pattern under a restrained melody. For a sad scene or a loss.

title: Prelude Op. 28 No. 20 (Chopin)
note: Twelve bars of solemn chords: very short, very strong. A funeral or a moment of silence; loops well because it is short.

title: Waltz in B minor, Op. 69 No. 2 (Chopin)
note: A wistful, elegant waltz.

title: Minute Waltz, Op. 64 No. 1 (Chopin)
note: A quick, sparkling waltz (about a minute, as the nickname says). The opening has a whirling figure; good for a lively comic scene.

title: Étude Op. 25 No. 1, "Aeolian Harp" (Chopin)
note: A constant wash of broken chords with a melody floating on top: shimmering water or wind. Use the lead and bass.

title: Étude Op. 10 No. 1 (Chopin)
note: Rolling arpeggios across the keyboard; an energetic, heroic motion. The lead is the top note of each arpeggio.

title: Étude Op. 25 No. 2, "The Bees" (Chopin)
note: A quick, murmuring figure like bees: fits a busy, light stage.

title: Waltz Op. 39 No. 15 (Brahms)
note: A gentle, famous little waltz. A model of a perfect eight-bar melody; sweet and simple.

title: Intermezzo Op. 118 No. 2 (Brahms)
note: A tender, autumnal piece with a warm melody.

title: The Seasons: January, "At the Fireside" (Tchaikovsky)
note: A cosy, warm tune for a fireside or an indoor winter scene.

title: The Seasons: February, "Carnival" (Tchaikovsky)
note: A lively carnival dance.

title: The Seasons: August, "Harvest" (Tchaikovsky)
note: A bustling harvest-time piece; fits a farm or a country fair.

title: Neapolitan Dance (Tchaikovsky, Swan Lake)
note: A showy dance that starts with a fanfare; good for a fair or a party stage.

title: Berceuse (Fauré, Dolly Suite)
note: A tender lullaby from the Dolly Suite. Very gentle.

title: Sonata No. 8 "Pathétique", 1st movement, Allegro (Beethoven)
note: After a slow, heavy introduction (the Grave, about 10 bars), the Allegro is driving, stormy and minor. This excerpt starts at the Allegro. Excellent boss or dungeon music.

title: Sonata No. 8 "Pathétique", 2nd movement, Adagio cantabile (Beethoven)
note: One of the most beautiful melodies of the period: a long, singing line. For an emotional ending.

title: Sonata No. 23 "Appassionata", 3rd movement (Beethoven)
note: Relentless, furious sixteenth-note motion. For a final battle or a desperate chase. Very busy: the lead will be dense.

title: Symphony No. 5 in C minor, piano reduction (Beethoven)
note: The short-short-short-long "fate" motif is the most recognisable four notes in classical music; the piano reduction carries the whole first movement. Use the motif as a leitmotif for a villain or a doom.

title: Symphony No. 25 in G minor, 1st movement (Mozart)
note: The "little G minor": restless, syncopated, urgent. A good boss or pursuit.

title: Erlkönig (Schubert)
note: A pounding, galloping triplet figure under a frightened melody. For a night chase or a haunting.

title: Der Tod und das Mädchen (Schubert)
note: A solemn, chordal theme (Death's reply is a slow hymn-like chord progression). For death, a graveyard, a solemn choice.

title: Quartettsatz in C minor, D. 703 (Schubert)
note: Restless tremolo and a driving theme; an urgent chase or escape.

title: Fantaisie-Impromptu (Chopin)
note: A flurry of fast notes with a rolling left hand; stormy and breathless. Use for a chase. Busy: the lead will be dense.

title: Marche funèbre in C minor, K. 453a (Mozart)
note: A slow funeral march.

title: La traviata, Preludio (Verdi)
note: The delicate, aching string prelude. For a sad ending or a quiet menu.

title: La traviata, Brindisi, the drinking song (Verdi)
note: The famous drinking song: a lilting waltz tune that everyone knows. Great for a party scene or a victory.

title: La traviata, Valzer e duetto (Verdi)
note: A waltz from the party scene.

title: La traviata, Coro di zingari, the gypsy chorus (Verdi)
note: A rhythmic, stamping chorus with a Spanish-gypsy colour; good for a camp or a market.

title: La traviata, Coro di mattadori spagnuoli, the bullfighters (Verdi)
note: A brisk, bright Spanish fanfare; a good arena or a festival title.

title: Piano Sonata No. 17 "Tempest", 1st movement (Beethoven)
note: A slow, searching opening (Largo) alternating with a stormy Allegro; tense and unsettled. Good for an uneasy exploration or a cave of danger.

title: String Quartet No. 4 in C minor, 1st movement (Beethoven)
note: A restless, driven C minor; the top line is the first violin.

title: Toccata and Fugue in D minor (J. S. Bach, organ)
note: The famous opening: a flourish, then long chords. The very start is the "villain appears" sting; the fugue after it is a moving, restless background. Use bars 1-5 as a sting and the fugue as music.

title: Polonaise in G minor (Anna Magdalena Notebook, BWV Anh. 119)
note: A stately little polonaise in minor; light and clear.
composer: Notebook for Anna Magdalena Bach (1725); composer uncertain, some pieces are by Bach's contemporaries

title: Minuet in A minor (Anna Magdalena Notebook, BWV Anh. 120)
note: A light minuet in A minor.
composer: Notebook for Anna Magdalena Bach (1725); composer uncertain, some pieces are by Bach's contemporaries

title: March in E-flat major (Anna Magdalena Notebook, BWV Anh. 127)
note: A clear, simple march.
composer: Notebook for Anna Magdalena Bach (1725); composer uncertain, some pieces are by Bach's contemporaries

title: Menuet (Anna Magdalena Notebook, BWV Anh. 113)
note: A short, simple minuet; very easy to loop.
composer: Notebook for Anna Magdalena Bach (1725); composer uncertain, some pieces are by Bach's contemporaries

title: Dies irae, from the Requiem (Mozart)
note: The "day of wrath": dark and urgent, in a choral texture (top voice as the tune). Use sparingly, as a doom or a boss sting.

title: Marche militaire No. 1 (Schubert)
note: The famous military march (the first of three): a crisp, dotted rhythm and a tune everyone half-knows. Marches loop well because the phrases are square. Good for a parade, a brisk title or a "soldiers set out" scene.

title: Bourrée in E minor, BWV 996 (J. S. Bach, lute)
note: A cheerful-but-minor dance on the lute; quick stepwise motion and a clear two-part texture that suits the lead and bass well. The minor key without gloom: a good tavern, a night market or a clever heist.

title: English Suite No. 1, Bourrée I (J. S. Bach)
note: A bright, steady dance with a clear tune: confident without being loud. A sturdy exploration or hub theme.

title: Gavotte (Handel)
note: A neat, courtly dance with a four-square tune: simple enough for a tutorial, polite enough for a castle hall.

title: In the Hall of the Mountain King (Grieg, Peer Gynt)
note: The famous creeping theme: the same short phrase repeated over a pedal bass, higher and faster each time. It begins softly (sneaking) and is meant to accelerate: start at this tempo and lower music_tempo every pass for a chase that gets out of hand.

title: March of the Dwarfs / Troldtog (Grieg)
note: A stomping, mischievous march with a chromatic twist: a good cave, mine or mountain-troll level. Lead and bass trade quickly.

title: Wedding Day at Troldhaugen (Grieg)
note: A joyful, flowing wedding piece with a singing tune. A bright title or a village celebration.

title: Åse's Death (Grieg, Peer Gynt)
note: A slow, solemn lament in strings: a funeral or a loss. Very simple and heavy; a tune for the saddest beat of a story.

title: Greensleeves (traditional, lute setting)
note: The old English ballad in a lute setting: a minor-mode lilt in 6/8. Familiar and warm. Use it for a tavern, an old town or a quiet reflective stage.

title: Red Apple Rag (traditional fiddle tune)
note: An American old-time fiddle tune: a bouncing, jig-like hoedown. For a farm, a barn dance or a cheerful caper.

title: Soldier's Joy (traditional fiddle tune)
note: A very old fiddle tune used for country dances in Britain and America. Quick, merry and instantly danceable.

title: Aamulla varhain (Finnish folk song)
note: A gentle Finnish folk song ("early in the morning"): a quiet, northern, folk-song feel for a village at dawn.

title: Oats and Beans and Barley Grow (traditional)
note: A simple English children's singing game: a bouncy, easy tune for a farm or an early, friendly level.

title: John Barleycorn (English folk song)
note: A strong English folk melody about the barley harvest; earthy and a little dark. A tavern or a harvest festival.

title: The Water of Tyne (northern English folk song)
note: A yearning ballad: a woman waiting for her love across the river. Slow and simple.

title: Flee as a Bird (traditional)
note: A plaintive, soaring melody; good for a quiet departure, a bird scene or an ending.

title: It's Me, O Lord (traditional spiritual)
note: A gospel spiritual in four parts: earnest and warm. For an ending, a memorial or a quiet moment of thanks.

title: New Britain, the tune of "Amazing Grace" (traditional)
note: The tune known as Amazing Grace: a pentatonic melody that is among the easiest in the world to remember. For an ending, a memorial or a gentle moment of hope.

title: Veni Emmanuel (O Come, O Come Emmanuel)
note: An old plainchant-derived tune in a minor mode, long and yearning. Winter, a procession, a quiet title.

title: The First Noel (traditional carol)
note: The carol, in four-part harmony. For a winter scene or a seasonal ending.

title: Good King Wenceslas (traditional carol tune)
note: A walking, wintry carol: the tune is steady and square, and loops well. A snowy journey.

title: The Holly and the Ivy (traditional carol)
note: A lilting English carol: a folk-dance feel in 3/4 or 6/8. A winter fair.

title: Dundee (Scottish psalm tune)
note: A sturdy old Scottish psalm tune: square and plain; a good memorial or a quiet title.

title: St. Denio (Welsh hymn tune)
note: A bright Welsh hymn tune ("Immortal, invisible"): confident and majestic.

title: Thaxted (Holst, the Jupiter tune)
note: The broad, noble tune from Holst's "Jupiter" set as a hymn: a royal, expansive theme. Holst died in 1934.

title: Tryggare kan ingen vara (Swedish hymn tune)
note: A plain, calm Swedish hymn tune; a peaceful ending.

title: Es ist ein Ros entsprungen (A Rose Has Sprung)
note: A tender German carol, in four parts. A quiet winter night.

title: La Chasse, Op. 100 No. 9 (Burgmüller)
note: A galloping hunting piece with horn-call figures in 6/8: forest, hunt, a light-hearted chase.

title: La Styrienne, Op. 100 No. 14 (Burgmüller)
note: A rustic Styrian dance: a lilting folk-dance melody. A village fair.

title: L'Arabesque, Op. 100 No. 2 (Burgmüller)
note: A light, quick piece in minor with a bouncing line; a good running or collecting stage.

title: La Pastorale, Op. 100 No. 3 (Burgmüller)
note: A gentle pastoral: shepherd's country feeling in 6/8.

title: La Bergeronnette, Op. 100 No. 21 (Burgmüller)
note: A tripping little piece: "the wagtail". A bird, a garden, a light stage.

title: Ballade, Op. 100 No. 15 (Burgmüller)
note: A story-telling piece with a minor opening and a bright turn: it suits a story-driven intro or a mystery.

title: L'Adieu, Op. 100 No. 12 (Burgmüller)
note: "The farewell": gentle and tender. A short farewell scene or an ending.

title: Le Courant Limpide, Op. 100 No. 7 (Burgmüller)
note: "The clear stream": a flowing, easy figure. Water, a river, a calm exploring stage.

title: La Babillarde, Op. 100 No. 4 (Burgmüller)
note: "The chatterbox": quick, light and talkative. A market, a gossip scene, a comic stage.

title: Inquiétude, Op. 100 No. 18 (Burgmüller)
note: "Restlessness": an anxious, rolling minor figure. A low-key tense stage.

title: Tendre Fleur, Op. 100 No. 10 (Burgmüller)
note: "Tender flower": sweet and gentle.

title: Scherzo in E minor (Mendelssohn)
note: Quick and airy: the sound of fairies and elves (Mendelssohn also wrote "A Midsummer Night's Dream"). A forest at night, a light chase.

title: Venetian Gondola Song, Op. 30 No. 6 (Mendelssohn)
note: A barcarolle: a rocking 6/8 gondola rhythm with a singing melody over it. A canal, a boat, a moonlit river.

title: Song Without Words Op. 53 No. 5, "Folk Song" (Mendelssohn)
note: A simple, folk-like melody over steady chords.

title: Song Without Words Op. 85 No. 1 (Mendelssohn)
note: A gently flowing song without words.

title: Thunder and Lightning Polka (Johann Strauss II)
note: A boisterous polka with thunder-claps: a comic storm, a frantic kitchen or a slapstick chase.

title: Sonata in C major (D. Scarlatti, harpsichord)
note: A bright, crisp harpsichord sonata: clear and tidy, a good tutorial or puzzle background.

title: Sonatina Op. 20 No. 1, Allegro (Kuhlau)
note: A neat, cheerful classical sonatina: a clear tune with simple harmony. A friendly early stage.

title: Sonatina Op. 20 No. 1, Rondo (Kuhlau)
note: A playful rondo: a bouncing tune that comes back. A good loop.

title: Les Sauvages (Rameau)
note: A rhythmic baroque dance depicting "savages": a stamping, catchy tune. A jungle, a tribal market, an expedition.

title: Les Tendres Plaintes (Rameau)
note: "The tender complaints": a sighing, gentle baroque rondeau.

title: Tambourin (Rameau)
note: A drone-bass dance imitating pipe and tabor: brisk and rustic.

title: Rondo (Pleyel)
note: A bright classical rondo: neat and friendly.

title: Rumores de la Caleta (Albéniz)
note: A Spanish malagueña: guitar-like repeated notes over a flamenco colour. A southern town or a beach evening.

title: Romanian Folk Dance (Bartók)
note: A stamping, angular folk dance with modal colour. A rural fair.

title: Echigo Jishi (Japanese lion dance, koto)
note: A traditional lion-dance piece: lively and rhythmic, in a pentatonic colour. A very different sound world from the European pieces; good for a festival or a Japanese-set stage.

title: Sakura-Miyotote (Japanese traditional, koto)
note: A traditional koto piece in a pentatonic mode: calm and open. Spring, a garden, a shrine.

title: Chidori Meimei (Japanese traditional, shamisen)
note: A shamisen piece named for plovers: light, plucked, sparse. A shore or a calm night.

title: Gonbe ga Tanemaku (Japanese folk song)
note: A Japanese folk song about a farmer sowing seeds: a simple, playful tune.
